chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Shihab! Killing will increase among a household from Quraish to the extent that a man from among them will be called to the Caliphate, and he will refuse it.' Then he said: 'O Shihab! Do not say that I meant these sons of my uncle.' Shihab said: 'I testify that he indeed meant them.'
ai.seo_question: Which household from Quraish did Imam al-Sadiq refer to when predicting increased killing and a refusal of Caliphate?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) foretells a period of intense civil strife and martyrdom within the Banu Umayya, culminating in a caliphate offer that is ultimately rejected. The Imam’s instruction to Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih to avoid explicitly naming the family highlights the scholarly principle of *kitman* (concealment) to prevent premature political identification or sectarian conflict before the prophesied events unfold. This narrative underscores the transition of authority from the Umayyads to the Ahl al-Bayt, framing their rise as a divine resolution to the preceding turmoil.
